summary: Describes the Terms of Reference of RIPE (Reseaux IP Europeens), the cooperation of European IP networks. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC describes RIPE, a coordinating body for European IP networks. It sets out RIPE's role in sharing technical information and coordinating interconnection while leaving each network under its own organization's authority.

tldr.problem: European IP networks were expanding beyond local networks and across national and international wide-area networks, creating a need for coordination.
tldr.mechanism: RIPE provides a forum for technical information, coordinates interconnection and common network-management practices, and supports other shared IP-networking activities.

sections.title: Why RIPE Was Created
sections.content:
RIPE stands for Réseaux IP Européens. The RFC says the coordinating body was created as IP networks expanded beyond local networks and across Europe through national and international wide-area networks.

Its objective is to provide administrative and technical coordination so a pan-European IP network can operate and expand.
sections.plainLanguage: RIPE was created to coordinate European IP networks as they connected across wider areas. The RFC sets out the body's objective and scope.

sections.title: RIPE's Responsibilities and Participation
sections.content:
RIPE acts as a forum for exchanging technical information and building expertise in IP networking. It promotes and coordinates interconnection within Europe and with other continents, and works toward agreement on common network-management practices.

Operators of wide-area IP networks are encouraged to participate. RIPE is not a service provider, and participating networks remain under the executive authority of their respective organizations. RIPE documents are publicly available.
sections.plainLanguage: RIPE helps network operators share information and coordinate connections and management practices. The operators keep authority over their own networks.

sections.title: Status and Scope
sections.content: RFC 1181 is an informational document describing RIPE's terms of reference. It does not specify a standard. Its stated area of relevance is Europe.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is an informational description of RIPE's role in Europe. It does not define a technical standard.
